facts.statement: The name Dicraeosaurus refers to the distinctive neural spines located on the back of the animal's neck.
facts.quote: The genus was named for the neural spines on the back of its neck.

facts.statement: The first fossils of Dicraeosaurus were described by paleontologist Werner Janensch in 1914.
facts.quote: The first fossil was described by paleontologist Werner Janensch in 1914.

facts.statement: Unlike most diplodocoids, Dicraeosaurus possessed a comparatively large head and a relatively short, wide neck.
facts.quote: Unlike most diplodocoids, Dicraeosaurus had a comparatively large head with a relatively short and wide neck.

facts.statement: The neck of Dicraeosaurus contained 12 unusually short vertebrae, suggesting it was a low-level browser feeding on vegetation no more than 3 meters off the ground.
facts.quote: The neck contained 12 unusually short vertebrae, likely indicating a low-level browser of vegetation no more than 3 m off the ground.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus was smaller than many other diplodocoids, measuring 14 to 15 meters in length and 5 to 6 metric tons, yet it remains one of the larger members of the family Dicraeosauridae.
facts.quote: It was smaller than many other diplodocoids, at only 14 - 15 m in length and 5 - 6 MT, though this still makes it among the larger known members of the family Dicraeosauridae.

facts.statement: The genus is notable for tall neural spines that formed a rough "Y" shape rather than being straight like in some other family members.
facts.quote: The genus is notable for the rather tall neural spines protruding from its vertebrae, which it is named for. They were not straight as in some members of the family, instead forming a rough "Y" shape.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the tall neural spines likely provided attachment points for muscles.
facts.quote: These spines likely provided muscle attachment points.

facts.statement: In 2008, Lehman and Woodward estimated that a mature adult Dicraeosaurus lived for 11 to 22 years and grew at an average rate of 227 to 455 kg per year.
facts.quote: In 2008, Lehman and Woodward estimated the minimum and maximum ages of a mature adult Dicraeosaurus at 11 to 22 years, and the average growth rate to be 227 - 455 kg per year.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus was a mid-sized herbivore found in the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania, which dates to the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Dicraeosaurus was a mid-sized herbivore for its ecosystem, found in the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania, which dates to the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus measured between 13 and 20 meters in length, up to 6 meters in height, and weighed 15 tons.
facts.quote: Dicraeosaurus medía entre 13 y 20 metros de largo y hasta 6 de alto, con un peso de 15 toneladas.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus had a long narrow tail, a spine-covered back, solid legs, a long head with long incisors in its jaws, and a neck built of only 12 vertebrae, which was shorter than those of other sauropods of its time.
facts.quote: Poseían una larga cola estrecha, un dorso con espinas, patas macizas y una cabeza larga con largos incisivos en sus mandíbulas, el cuello estaba construido con solo 12 vértebras, siendo más corto que los de los otros saurópodos de su época.

facts.statement: Unlike most diplodocoids, Dicraeosaurus had a relatively large head because its neck was shorter and wider.
facts.quote: A diferencia de la mayoría de los diplodocoides Dicraeosaurus tenía una cabeza relativamente grande puesto que su cuello era más corto y más ancho.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus lacked the whip-like tail tip typical of diplodocoids.
facts.quote: También careció la cola en forma de látigo que los diplodócidos tenían.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Dicraeosaurus had a Y-shape, resembling a bifurcation.
facts.quote: Cada una tenía una forma de Y, como una bifurcación.

facts.statement: These spines served as insertion points for powerful neck muscles.
facts.quote: Estás espinas sirvieron como puntos de inserción para poderoso músculos del cuello.

facts.statement: A short fourth trochanter is present on the lateral side of the femur bone.
facts.quote: En la parte superior del hueso del muslo en el lado lateral hay un cuarto trocánter corto.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus lived during the late Jurassic period, approximately 156 to 145 million years ago, between the Oxfordian and Tithonian stages, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente hace 156 a 145 millones de años, entre el Oxfordiense y el Titoniense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The genus Dicraeosaurus has been synonymized with Issasaurus, Mtotosaurus, Nyororosaurus, and Selimanosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: "Issasaurus" Maier 2003 "Mtotosaurus" Maier 2003 "Nyororosaurus" Maier 2003 "Selimanosaurus" Maier 2003

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus could reach up to 20 meters in length, of which 2.4 meters belonged to the neck.
facts.quote: Dicraeosaurus tenía hasta 20 metros de largo, de los cuales 2,4 metros pertenecen al cuello.

facts.statement: Numerous attempts to estimate its mass yielded varied results, placing the mass of D. hansemanni between 10 and 40 tons.
facts.quote: Numerosos intentos de estimar su masa arrojaron resultados variados, colocando la masa de D. hansemanni entre 10 y 40 toneladas.

facts.statement: Calculations indicate that Dicraeosaurus contained 974 liters of air, with a 48-kilogram heart pumping 641 liters of blood at a rate of 23 beats per minute.
facts.quote: En Dicraeosaurus contenían 974 litros de aire. Los cálculos muestran que 641 litros de sangre se bombeaban por un corazón que pesaba 48 kilogramos latiendo 23 veces por minuto.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus grew rapidly and without interruption to its maximum size, reaching sexual maturity at 80% of that maximum size.
facts.quote: Dicraeosaurus creció rápidamente y sin interrupción hasta su tamaño máximo. Alcanzando el 80 % de este tamaño máximo, maduraba sexualmente.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Dicraeosaurus stopped growing earlier than its relatives is supported by the poor pneumatization of its bones.
facts.quote: Esta hipótesis también se sostiene por la pobre neumatización de sus huesos

facts.statement: The peg-shaped teeth of Dicraeosaurus were ideal for feeding on plants.
facts.quote: Sus dientes con forma de clavijas son ideales para alimentarse de las plantas.

facts.statement: While some authors suggest the skull structure indicates biting movements adapted for cutting food, others interpret it as front-to-back movements typical of earlier sauropods adapted for pulling food.
facts.quote: Al igual que la estructura del cráneo, que apuntan a la inclinación de los movimientos de las mordidas durante la comida, otros autores ver aquí los movimientos de la parte delantera-trasera, que se producía en diplodocoides más adaptado para cortar alimentos que para arrancarlos como anteriores saurópodos.

facts.statement: There is a crest or comb-like structure on the back of the head.
facts.quote: Hay un peine en la parte posterior de la cabeza.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus had up to 12 cervical vertebrae containing numerous air spaces, especially developed at the back of the neck.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales de este animal, que en Dicraeosauridae no es superior en el número a 12, mostraron numerosos espacios aéreos, más desarrollado en la parte posterior del cuello.

facts.statement: The tibia of Dicraeosaurus measured 79 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: en el que la tibia mide los 79 centímetros.

facts.statement: The bifurced neural spines of Dicraeosaurus reached a length of more than four times the height of the body.
facts.quote: Las apófisis espinosas se bifurcan, alcanzando una longitud de más de cuatro veces la altura que cuerpo.

facts.statement: The genus name Dicraeosaurus means "forked lizard" due to its bifurcated neural spines.
facts.quote: Guiado por esta característica de las vértebras, al animal se le dio el nombre genérico Dicraeosaurus que significa "lagarto bifurcado".

facts.statement: The first fossil of Dicraeosaurus was described by Werner Janensch in 1914.
facts.quote: El primer fósil fue descrito por Werner Janensch en 1914.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dicraeosaurus were found in the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania and possibly in Kazdi, Zimbabwe.
facts.quote: Se encontraron fósiles en la Formación Tendaguru en Tanzania y probablemente también de Kazdi en Zimbabue.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus was discovered during German expeditions to the Tendaguru site in Tanzania between 1909 and 1913.
facts.quote: Dicraeosaurus proviene del famoso sitio de Tendaguru en Tanzania y fue encontrado durante las expediciones alemanas de 1909 a 1913.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus hansemanni lived between the Oxfordian and Kimeridgian stages, while D. sattleri lived during the Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: Dicraeosaurus hansemanni en la Inferior y Media entre el Oxfordiano y el Kimeridgiano y Dicraeosaurus sattleri en la Superior del Titoniano.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus lived from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian stages, approximately 161.5 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Tithonian (161.5 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers Martin and colleagues suggest that a cervical ligament played a decisive role in maintaining the neck position.
facts.quote: Según Martin y colaboradores, el papel decisivo en el mantenimiento del cuello sería un ligamento cervical.

facts.statement: It is suggested that Dicraeosaurus maintained an upright neck and bent head while walking on extended legs.
facts.quote: Se notó que los animales de hoy que caminan sobre patas estiradas generalmente mantienen el cuello erguido y doblan la cabeza. Esto también debería aplicarse a Dicraeosaurus.

facts.statement: Some experts believe the neck of Dicraeosaurus could have been inclined, though a horizontal position is not excluded.
facts.quote: Otros expertos creen que el cuello también podría inclinarse, pero no excluyen una posición horizontal.

facts.statement: The long neck of sauropods like Dicraeosaurus may have evolved as a result of sexual selection.
facts.quote: El cuello largo de los saurópodos también podría ser el resultado de la selección sexual.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus was a herbivore that did not compete with other dinosaurs for food.
facts.quote: Era herbívoro, sin embargo, no compitió con otros dinosaurios para la comida.

facts.statement: Dicraeosaurus could eat hard foods like cycads thanks to its wide teeth.
facts.quote: gracias a sus dientes anchos, pudieron comer alimentos duros, como cícadas.

facts.statement: Since 1991, Dicraeosaurus has been classified in the family Dicraeosauridae, part of the superfamily Diplodocoidea.
facts.quote: Desde 1991 se lo ha colocado Dicraeosauridae, que es parte de la superfamilia Diplodocoide.

facts.statement: The family Dicraeosauridae is believed to be more evolutionarily advanced than the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: Se cree que la familia Dicraeosauridae es más avanzada en la evolución que la familia Diplodocidae.

facts.statement: A 2005 study by Rauhut confirmed that Dicraeosaurus is monophyletic and more closely related to Brachytrachelopan than to Amargasaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en el estudio de 2005 Rauhut confirmó el tipo de monofilia, así como su relación más cercana a Brachytrachelopan que a Amargasaurus.

facts.statement: Further studies are needed to confirm the systematic classification of this group.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, se observa que es necesario llevar a cabo más estudios que confirmen la sistemática de este grupo.

facts.statement: The tail of Dicraeosaurus, which acted like a whip, could be used for defense or to make loud sounds.
facts.quote: Se podría usar para defender o hacer sonidos fuertes.

facts.statement: The two species of Dicraeosaurus did not live together, as they were found in different geological layers spanning from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian.
facts.quote: Los dos tipos de Dicraeosaurus por lo tanto no vivían juntos, se encontraron en diferentes capas, Dicraeosaurus hansemanni en la Inferior y Media entre el Oxfordiano y el Kimeridgiano y Dicraeosaurus sattleri en la Superior del Titoniano.

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Beeston et al. included Dicraeosaurus sattleri in an analysis of caudal vertebrae that found at least five independent origins or reversals of pneumaticity in Neosauropoda.
facts.quote: A study on the caudal vertebrae of Cetiosaurus sp., "Cetiosaurus" glymptonensis, Wamweracaudia keranjei, Dicraeosaurus sattleri, Tornieria africana and Giraffatitan brancai, providing evidence of at least five independent origins and/or reversals of pneumaticity of anterior caudal vertebrae in Neosauropoda, is published by Beeston et al. (2026).
